label: DEEP-RESEARCH TASK: the CRUX — SOCIAL + MEDIA app embed feasibility in 2026. For EACH of:

findings.summary: The single most important honest finding: the "social wall" is NOT a simple iframe anymore, and the split is stark. Video/newer platforms (YouTube, Vimeo, Twitch, TikTok single-video, Bluesky, Threads, Pinterest, Snapchat single-item) still offer working official iframe/oEmbed embeds an operator can use unattended — these ride our existing STREAMING/WEBPAGE widgets at S effort. But the three platforms operators most want on a lobby wall — Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn — have effectively KILLED unattended public embeds: Meta shut down Instagram Basic Display (Dec 2024), deprecated the token-free oEmbed (Oct/Nov 2025 → Meta oEmbed Read now requires an app-reviewed access token + Business/Creator account), and LinkedIn never offered a company-feed embed at all (one-post-at-a-time, no auto-update). X/Twitter is a special case: the old widgets.js timeline still loads with NO key but is now intermittently blank/unreliable in 2026, and the API went pay-per-use in Feb 2026 with NO free tier for new devs. Reviews (Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor) have no official display-embed and are gated behind APIs with hard review-count caps (3-7) and caching restrictions. This is exactly why every signage vendor (OptiSigns, Yodeck, ScreenCloud) quietly leans on PAID 3rd-party aggregators (EmbedSocial, Curator.io, Walls.io, Juicer, Taggbox, Flockler) for the "hard" networks — the aggregator holds the OAuth/business-account/API-key burden and hands back one embeddable URL. Recommendation: build a curated Apps library where the EASY 8 are native S-effort configs on our own widgets, and the HARD networks (IG/FB/LinkedIn + reviews) route through ONE pluggable aggregator connector (operator brings/pays for an aggregator, or we resell) rather than promising a fake native embed we can't keep alive.

apps.name: Instagram
apps.howEmbedded2026: PUBLIC EMBED IS DEAD for unattended use. Basic Display API shut down Dec 4 2024. Token-free oEmbed deprecated Oct 1 / extended Nov 3 2025 — Meta oEmbed Read now REQUIRES an app-reviewed access token (client or app token) + the account must be Business/Creator and use Instagram Graph API/Login. Single public post oEmbed technically works but loses thumbnail_url/author fields and needs the reviewed app+token. Realistic signage path in 2026 = a PAID 3rd-party aggregator (EmbedSocial/Curator/Walls.io/Juicer/Taggbox) that holds the OAuth+business-account plumbing and returns one embeddable feed URL. NO simple iframe.
apps.notes: The #1 requested lobby wall AND the hardest. OptiSigns ships separate 'Instagram' and 'Instagram Business' apps precisely because personal accounts can't feed anymore; they moderate via Business login. Do NOT promise a raw-URL iframe — it will silently die.

apps.name: Facebook (Page)
apps.howEmbedded2026: Page Plugin/oEmbed still renders public Pages/posts BUT is now under Meta oEmbed Read: apps created after Apr 8 2025 need the reviewed 'meta_oembed_read' feature + access token; author_name/author_url stripped from responses. Legacy no-token oEmbed deprecated on the Oct/Nov 2025 timeline. A continuously-refreshing Page feed for signage realistically needs Graph API + a Page access token (admin-connected) or a paid aggregator. Single public post embed is the only near-simple path and still needs the token.
apps.notes: Same Meta gate as Instagram; connect them together (IG Business links to a FB Page). Aggregator is the pragmatic answer for a live wall.

apps.name: LinkedIn (Company Page)
apps.howEmbedded2026: NO official company-feed embed — never existed and LinkedIn killed public page plugins years ago. Native embed = ONE post at a time (desktop only, visibility must be 'Anyone'), and it does NOT auto-update. A live company feed on signage is ONLY achievable via a paid aggregator (EmbedSocial/Walls.io/Juicer/Taggbox), which refreshes on the tool's schedule, not instantly.
apps.notes: High-value for CORPORATE vertical, but there is genuinely no first-party path. Aggregator-only. Frame it honestly.

apps.name: X / Twitter
apps.howEmbedded2026: Two paths, both compromised. (1) Legacy widgets.js from platform.twitter.com still loads a timeline/single-tweet with NO API key — but in 2026 it's intermittently blank, delayed, and inconsistent across browsers (failures compound with multiple embeds); publish.twitter.com produces broken markup. (2) Official API went PAY-PER-USE Feb 6 2026 with NO free tier for new devs ($0.005/post read, capped 2M/mo; legacy Basic $200/mo & Pro $5k/mo being auto-migrated off). So a reliable X wall = paid API OR a paid aggregator. The free iframe path exists but you cannot promise reliability.
apps.notes: Offer the no-key widgets.js embed as a best-effort 'may go blank' single-tweet/timeline app (S), but for a dependable feed it's aggregator/API (L). OptiSigns kept a 'Twitter Counter' app, telling — they downgraded to metadata not live feed.

apps.name: TikTok
apps.howEmbedded2026: Single-video embed WORKS unattended: official oEmbed API (URL → HTML) + an iframe player (query params to hide controls/description). Standard oEmbed-spec compliant, no OAuth for a public video embed. A continuously-updating account/hashtag FEED, however, needs the TikTok Display API (OAuth) or a paid aggregator — the free path is per-video only.
apps.notes: Single-video = easy STREAMING/EXTERNAL_HTML embed. Feed = aggregator. Autoplay/mute behavior varies on locked-down players; verify on Taurus.

apps.name: YouTube
apps.howEmbedded2026: SIMPLE IFRAME, still the gold standard. youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID, /embed/videoseries?list=PLAYLIST_ID (best for signage — update the playlist, screen follows), and /embed/live_stream?channel=CHANNEL_ID for live. Caveats: content must be PUBLIC (not unlisted/private); channel /live links embed unreliably; only one scheduled public live at a time or the channel embed breaks; nothing is downloaded so it needs a live network connection (no offline).
apps.notes: We already have this via STREAMING. Add polished per-app config: video vs playlist vs live-channel, autoplay+mute (required for autoplay), loop, controls-off. Playlist mode is the killer signage feature.

apps.name: LinkedIn
apps.notes: Duplicate of the Company Page entry; keep one card in the UI.

apps.name: Twitch
apps.howEmbedded2026: OFFICIAL IFRAME EMBED works (live channel, VOD, clips, or chat). Two hard requirements: the embedding domain MUST be served over SSL/HTTPS, and you MUST pass a &parent=DOMAIN param listing every domain it renders on (as a JS array for multiple). This is the catch for signage — our player domain(s) must be enumerated. Autoplay+muted supported.
apps.notes: The &parent requirement is the whole ballgame: our config form must inject the correct player-domain(s). If we serve player content from a null-origin/sandboxed iframe or multiple hosts, plan for it. Otherwise trivial.

apps.name: Vimeo
apps.howEmbedded2026: SIMPLE IFRAME, cleanest of all. player.vimeo.com/video/ID with autoplay/muted/loop/background params; oEmbed available (incl. private videos with token). Domain-level privacy ('specific domains' allowlist) on Standard+ plans — if the video owner restricts domains, our player domain must be listed. Standard+ also hides the Vimeo logo/controls for a clean signage look.
apps.notes: Best-behaved premium video source for signage (no ads, clean chrome, background mode). Config: paste URL/ID, autoplay+mute, loop, background. Warn if owner has domain-restrict on.

apps.name: Pinterest
apps.howEmbedded2026: OFFICIAL WIDGET BUILDER still works in 2026 — Pin, Board, and Profile widgets. Requires loading Pinterest's pinit.js script + an anchor with data attributes (so a small script shim, not a pure iframe, but no OAuth/API key for public boards/profiles). Board/Profile widgets auto-populate from public content.
apps.notes: Needs pinit.js — bake into an EXTERNAL_HTML board (script allowed in our sandboxed board pattern) rather than a bare src iframe. No token = low risk. Nice for RETAIL/FASHION/HOSPITALITY inspiration walls.

apps.name: Snapchat
apps.howEmbedded2026: Official Web Embeds exist for Spotlight videos, Public Stories, Public Profiles, and Lenses — copy the share-sheet 'embed' code (script/iframe snippet), no API key for public content. BUT you cannot embed an ephemeral Snap, and there is no simple auto-refreshing 'my account feed' — it's per-public-item. Public Profile API (OAuth) exists for metadata but isn't a display embed.
apps.notes: Low demand for signage; single-item embeds only. Deprioritize vs IG/FB/YouTube. Include as a paste-embed app if at all.

apps.name: Google Business / Reviews
apps.howEmbedded2026: NO official Google review-embed widget for business owners. Native options: a Maps embed (shows a map, not a clean review wall) or the Places API. Places API caps you at ~5 reviews per location, requires displaying attributions, and its ToS PROHIBIT caching/storing review content (only place_id is cacheable indefinitely) — a real problem for offline/locked-down players. Practical clean review wall = a paid 3rd-party widget/aggregator (EmbedSocial, Jotform, Taggbox, review-widget.net) that connects via Places API and hands back an embeddable, auto-syncing widget.
apps.notes: High value across QSR/RETAIL/HOSPITALITY. 5-review cap + no-cache ToS means we either build a Places-API connector (M, with caching-ToS care + attribution) or route to an aggregator (L). Do NOT scrape Google Maps — takedown risk.

apps.name: Yelp
apps.howEmbedded2026: NO public copy-paste embed. Yelp Fusion API only: free tier returns just 3 review EXCERPTS per business (Pro Premium = 7), keys must be server-side (never client-exposed), strict rate limits, and you may see fewer reviews than the live page. So a Yelp wall = Fusion API connector OR a paid aggregator (EmbedSocial/Tagembed/Elfsight) that wraps Fusion. Excerpts only, never full reviews.
apps.notes: 3-excerpt cap makes a satisfying wall hard first-party. Server-side key handling required (fits our server-side-proxy pattern like GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY). Aggregator likely the better ship.

apps.name: Tripadvisor
apps.howEmbedded2026: Tripadvisor offers official copy-paste WIDGETS (latest reviews, awards/ratings badges) from tripadvisor.com/Widgets for public listings — a genuine no-API embed path, though limited/branded and review count is capped. The Review Express API is for COLLECTING reviews (sending guest emails), NOT displaying them; a display API key is separate via tripadvisor.com/developers. For a richer custom wall, paid aggregators (SociableKit, Embeddable, Shapo, WP plugins) wrap it.
apps.notes: Better first-party story than Google/Yelp thanks to the official widget builder. Good for HOSPITALITY. Note the Review Express vs display-API distinction so we don't wire the wrong endpoint.

apps.name: Threads
apps.howEmbedded2026: Official Threads oEmbed exists (developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/reference/oembed) for PUBLIC posts, part of Meta oEmbed Read. Sources conflict on the token: Meta's marketing says 'embed public FB/Threads/IG without an access token,' but the Meta oEmbed Read framework generally requires a reviewed app + token, and the Threads reference page doesn't state a token-free guarantee. Single-post embed only — no simple auto-updating account feed without the API/aggregator. Treat as token-likely, single-item.
apps.notes: Same Meta ecosystem/gate as IG/FB but newer and lower demand. If we build the Meta oEmbed Read connector for IG/FB, Threads comes nearly free. Verify token requirement empirically before shipping token-free.

apps.name: Bluesky
apps.howEmbedded2026: GENUINELY SIMPLE and open. Official oEmbed at embed.bsky.app/oembed (accepts bsky.app URL or AT-URI, maxwidth 220-600), plus embed.bsky.app helper that returns a blockquote + script that upgrades to an iframe rendering the live post (media/quote-posts included). Auto-discovery via page metadata. NO API key, NO business account. Web-component options exist for full FEED widgets too.
apps.notes: The one social network that behaves the way IG/FB used to. Cheapest win in the whole set — single post is trivial, and open web-components can do a live feed. Great 'we support Bluesky' differentiator vs OptiSigns.

uxNotes: OptiSigns ships 140+ apps at $10/screen/mo and, tellingly, splits by capability rather than by brand vanity: it has BOTH an 'Instagram' and a separate 'Instagram Business' app because personal accounts can no longer feed — the app catalog itself encodes the Meta API reality. Our picker should do the same: don't show one generic 'Instagram' tile that lies; show what actually works (Business-connected feed vs single public post).

The dominant vendor pattern for the HARD networks is to NOT embed them directly — OptiSigns, Yodeck, ScreenCloud all offer a built-in content-moderation/approval step for social feeds, which is the giveaway that a real API/aggregator is fetching posts server-side (you can't moderate a raw iframe). If we do social feeds properly, we get a moderation queue almost for free and it becomes a selling point (schools especially want approve-before-display).

Aggregators (Walls.io, EmbedSocial, Curator.io, Juicer, Taggbox, Flockler) are the industry's shared dirty secret: they each pull a superset (Walls.io lists IG, FB, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, Bluesky, YouTube, Mastodon, Flickr, Pinterest, Vimeo, Reddit, Tumblr, RSS) and hand back ONE embeddable social-wall URL. The winning UX is: operator connects/pays an aggregator once, we render its wall URL in our WEBPAGE/EXTERNAL_HTML widget. This turns 8 impossible native integrations into one connector.

Every reviews platform (Google, Yelp, Tripadvisor) is API-gated with a hard per-location review cap (Google ~5, Yelp 3-7, Tripadvisor capped) — so the polished UX is a 'Reviews' app category with a rating-badge + rotating-excerpt layout designed AROUND the cap, not a scrolling infinite wall the API can't fill.

The single-item vs feed distinction is the most important UX fork: TikTok, Snapchat, Threads, Bluesky, X all embed a SINGLE public post/video trivially, but an auto-refreshing account FEED is a different (harder, often paid) integration. The picker should let the operator choose 'one post' (easy, free, instant) vs 'live feed' (connect account / aggregator) so expectations are set up front.

Video platforms deserve rich per-app config, not a URL box: YouTube needs video-vs-playlist-vs-live-channel mode + autoplay+mute (mandatory for browser autoplay) + loop + controls-off; Twitch needs the &parent domain injected automatically; Vimeo needs background/loop/hide-logo. A generic STREAMING widget hides these — a named app surfaces them as friendly toggles.

Reliability disclosure is a UX feature here: X's free widgets.js goes blank intermittently in 2026, YouTube channel /live links are flaky, Google/Yelp show fewer reviews than the live page. A trustworthy picker shows a small honesty badge per app ('Best effort — may occasionally not load' / 'Live feed requires connecting your account') rather than pretending every tile is bulletproof — this directly serves the CLAUDE.md 'no costumes' rule.
doBetterIdeas: Ship a two-tier Apps library that's HONEST by construction: Tier-A 'Native' apps (YouTube, Vimeo, Twitch, Bluesky, Pinterest, TikTok-single, Snapchat-single, Threads-single) as polished S-effort configs on our existing STREAMING/EXTERNAL_HTML/SOCIAL_FEED widgets; Tier-B 'Connected feeds' (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X live feed, all Reviews) that route through ONE pluggable aggregator connector. No fake native tile that silently dies — this is the CLAUDE.md 'no costumes' rule applied to the app marketplace.

Build ONE 'Social Wall' connector that abstracts a single aggregator (start with one — Walls.io or EmbedSocial have the widest source list incl. Bluesky), so the operator connects/pays once and gets IG+FB+LinkedIn+X+TikTok+reviews in one wall. This collapses ~8 impossible native integrations into a single maintainable connector, and the Integration Concierge can auto-detect their handles from the pasted website and pre-fill it.

Let the AI Concierge do the account-connection heavy lifting: paste your website → we scrape your IG/FB/LinkedIn/Google-Business handles and Yelp/Tripadvisor listing → Concierge proposes the exact apps + tells you plainly which need a Business account or aggregator, and pre-seeds a branded template. Turns the hardest, most IT-consultant-y part (OAuth + business-account + API keys) into a guided one-pass — directly on the operator-vision north star.

Own the moderation layer the incumbents bolt on: because Tier-B feeds fetch server-side, add an approve-before-display queue by default (huge for K-12/school walls and worship). OptiSigns/Yodeck treat this as a feature; we can make it the default and safer.

Design Reviews apps AROUND the API caps instead of fighting them: a 'Reviews' category with rating-badge + rotating-excerpt + overall-star layouts sized for 3-7 reviews, respecting Google's no-cache ToS by fetching live server-side through our existing GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY-style proxy and showing required attributions. Beats a half-empty scrolling wall.

Make our video apps out-config the field: YouTube playlist-mode ('add to the playlist, the screen follows') + auto mute/loop, Twitch with &parent auto-injected from the player domain, Vimeo background/clean-chrome — all as friendly toggles. These are the embeds that genuinely still work unattended, so nail the polish and lean on them in demos.

Lead with Bluesky as a differentiator: it's the ONE network that still embeds openly (no key, no business account, official oEmbed + open web-components for full feeds). OptiSigns/Yodeck don't feature it — 'first-class Bluesky wall' is a cheap, credible 'we're current' story.

Add a per-app 'reliability & requirements' badge and a live health check: 'Works unattended' / 'May occasionally not load (X)' / 'Requires Business account' / 'Requires connecting an aggregator' — plus a background pinger that flips the app to a friendly degraded state if the embed goes blank (X/YouTube-live), instead of showing a broken black box on a customer's wall. Turns the ecosystem's fragility into visible trustworthiness.
